issues.legal_issue: The limitation period for an auction purchaser’s application for possession begins when a pending challenge in the execution proceedings that could affect the sale is finally disposed of.
material_facts: A decree-holder purchased immovable property at an execution auction, and the sale was confirmed.
The judgment-debtor challenged the refusal to appoint a commissioner to assess the property’s value, and a stay of further execution proceedings remained in force while that revision was pending.
The revision was dismissed, and the purchaser applied for possession within one year of its disposal.
The High Court treated the confirmation date as the starting point and held the possession application time-barred.
issues.conclusion: The sale did not become absolute until the revision was disposed of. The possession application, filed within one year of that disposal, was within limitation; the High Court’s contrary order was set aside and the application restored to the executing court for disposal according to law.
issues.legal_principle: Article 134 of the Limitation Act, 1963 provides a one-year period for an application by a purchaser for possession of immovable property sold in execution of a decree, running from when the sale becomes absolute. Under Order XXI Rule 92(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure, a sale becomes absolute upon confirmation where no relevant application is made or such an application is disallowed. Applying Chandra Mani Saha v. Anarjan Bibi (AIR 1934 PC 134), as reiterated in Sri Ranga Nilayan Rama Krishna Rao v. Kandokori Chellayamma (AIR 1953 SC 425), a challenge that may affect whether the sale stands prevents the sale from becoming absolute until that challenge is disposed of. The Court left open whether issuance of a sale certificate is a prerequisite to filing the possession application and whether Section 15(1) of the Limitation Act applies.

rule.if: auction_possession_application and sale_confirmed and execution_challenge_pending and challenge_could_affect_sale and application_filed_within_one_year_after_challenge_disposed

predicates.auction_possession_application: A purchaser at an execution auction applied to the executing court for possession of the purchased property.
predicates.sale_confirmed: The executing court confirmed the auction sale.
predicates.execution_challenge_pending: The judgment-debtor pursued a challenge to an order made in the execution proceedings, and that challenge remained pending after confirmation of the sale.
predicates.challenge_could_affect_sale: The pending challenge could have resulted in the auction sale being set aside.
predicates.application_filed_within_one_year_after_: The purchaser filed the possession application within one year after the pending challenge was disposed of.

issues.definition: When a purchaser seeks possession after a confirmed execution sale, a pending challenge that could undo the sale means the application is within limitation if it is filed within one year after that challenge is disposed of.
